To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attachment of Corynebacteium parvum whole organisms to the surface of mouse macrophages is inhibited by HCl and lipid extracts of the organism, by sugars that are major components of its cell wall, and by removal of divalent cation from the medium.
the attachment of Corynebacteium parvum organisms to the surface of mouse macrophages in vitro was inhibited by HCl extracts and lipid extracts of C. parvm and by various sugars.

the binding of C. parum to glass-adhered mouse peritoneal cells is inhibited by HCl extract and lipid extract of the organisms, trypsinization of the cells does not affect the binding, the binding is inhibited by sugars and is dependent upon divalent cations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible mechanism by which the immunomodulatory effects of the organism may be mediated.
a possible mechanism of the activation of macrophages by C. parvun.
the mechanism of the activation of macrophages by the immunomodulatory agent, Corynebacterinum parvum, which is an extract of Corynebacteria species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

C. parvun is a potent immunomodulator and that its mode of action is not through the classical immunological mechanisms of antigen presentation, but rather through a non-specific activation of macrophages.
the attachment of organisms to the plasma membrane is not mediated by cell-bound antibody.
the binding of C. par. to glass-adherent cells is a specific interaction between the organism and the cells, and that it is mediated by divalent cations and a cell surface receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C. parvums are able to bind to the plasma membrane receptor on macrophages and that the attachment is mediated by divalent cations.
C. parvun binds to the cell surface via its cell wall components and that the binding is not antibody-mediated.

the binding of C. par. to the plasma membrane is a multivalent interaction of a complex cell wall component of the organism with a cell surface receptor on the macrophage, and that this binding is a prerequisite for the subsequent events of phagocytosis and macrophage activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C. parvums are not the most effective way to bind to the plasma membrane.
the C. parvums are not the only organisms that are capable of binding to the cell membrane.
the attachment of organisms is not affected by tryspin treatment of the cells.
